title: Exposure brief and ceremony templates for cross‑functional canaries (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc is an operational brief and grab-bag of lightweight ceremony/comm templates intended to help product + eng + SRE coordinate safe cross-functional canaries and small-batch A/B experiments. It is intentionally pragmatic: minimal ceremony, clear escalation, and reusable Slack/email snippets so teams can run experiments without reinventing the handshake every time.

Goals:
- Reduce friction for fast, controlled exposure of LLM-powered features.
- Ensure clear ownership across product/eng/sre/obs/safety.
- Provide signal-first stoplight rules and communication cadence to avoid surprise rollbacks.

When to use this doc:
- Any progressive rollout, microcanary, or targeted A/B slice involving model changes, rerankers, or behavioral guards that could affect end user content.
- Particularly for multi-team releases where human-in-the-loop observation or content safety checks are required.

Quick glossary (short):
- Exposure window: planned duration for initial traffic (e.g., 30m, 2h).
- Microcohort: small, predefined user slice (e.g., 1% new users, internal-only alpha).
- Steward: person actively monitoring the experiment during exposure window.

Ceremony checklist (pre-activation) — run 60–20 minutes before open: (tick boxes for steward)
- [ ] Hypothesis statement added to experiment ticket (what we expect to change).
- [ ] Primary and secondary signals enumerated (latency, error-rate, safety-flag-rate, quality scoring).
- [ ] Owner & backup steward assigned with contact info.
- [ ] Instrumentation links (dashboards, logs, traces) added to ticket.
- [ ] Slack channel created or chosen (narrow-scoped channel e.g., #rollout-dbr-134).
- [ ] Synthetic traffic plan (if any) indexed and smoke playbook ready.
- [ ] Canary slice and percent specification added to routing config.
- [ ] Rollback criteria documented (numeric thresholds + manual triggers).
- [ ] On-call SRE notified and included in the channel.

Activation cadence (sample)
1) T-15m: steward posts pre-flight summary in channel (see template A).
2) T=0: route first micro-slice (1% or internal-only) and mark timestamp.
3) T+10m: steward posts initial metrics snapshot.
4) T+30m: decision checkpoint — continue to next slice, pause, or rollback.
5) Iterate until full rollout or exit.

Signal prioritization (primary -> secondary)
- Safety flags (automated content moderation triggers, high severity) — immediate stoplight.
- Error / 5xx rate delta > 0.5% absolute — quick attention.
- Latency p50/p95 shifts (>= 30% increase in p95) — guardrail.
- Quality regressions on golden prompts (user-defined eval) — manual review.
- Cost per request anomalies (sudden spike) — ops check.

Stoplight rules (shorthand):
- GREEN: no threshold breaches after 30m, proceed to next slice.
- YELLOW: non-safety anomalies or marginal regressions — hold, run targeted investigation for 10–30m.
- RED: safety trigger OR critical latency/error spike — rollback immediately and page.

Roles and responsibilities (one-liners):
- Product owner: hypothesis, acceptance criteria, business impact.
- Steward (release lead): runs the ceremony, posts updates, executes pause/rollback.
- SRE/Infra on-call: supports rollback & capacity/fallback routing.
- Observability lead: validates telemetry and surface-failure triage.
- Safety reviewer: triages content flags; recommended for any language/generative change.

Observation scripts (quick commands / queries to run in first 30m)
- Query 1 (error surface): SELECT count(*) from requests where route=canary AND status>=500 GROUP BY 5m
- Query 2 (safety hits): filter moderation logs for canary route; sample top 10 flagged outputs
- Query 3 (latency buckets): p50/p95 for canary vs baseline by 5m window
- Golden prompt eval: run 5 golden prompts and post diffs in thread (use local eval harness link)

Slack templates (copy/paste editable)
- Template A: Pre-flight (T-15m)
"
:rotating_light: Canary pre-flight: ROLL-1123 — micro-slice -> 1% (internal users). Steward: @mariana_c. Owners: @ethan @priya. Hypothesis: reduce hallucination on support summarization w/o increasing latency. Primary signals: safety-flag-rate, p95 latency. Dashboards: <link>. Rollback criteria: safety flag > 0.5% OR p95 > baseline * 1.3 OR 5xx delta > 0.5%. On-call: @sre_oncall_team. We plan T=0 in 15m.
"
- Template B: Activation notice (T=0)
"
:rocket: Canary activation (T=0) — routing 1% to canary variant. Timestamp: <iso_ts>. Steward monitoring. Please post anything urgent in this channel.
"
- Template C: Yellow alert (hold/investigate)
"
:warning: OBSERVATION — holding at current exposure. Observed: p95 latency +35% vs baseline; safety flags unchanged. Actions: @obs_lead to deep-dive logs; @sre to confirm instance health; steward to pause growth until next checkpoint (T+30m).
"
- Template D: Immediate rollback (RED)
"
:rotating_light::exclamation: ROLLBACK — safety threshold breached (X flagged items) OR 5xx spike detected. Rolling back to stable variant and re-routing traffic. Steward executing. Paging: @sre_pager, @eng_lead. Postmortem follow-up ticket will be filed.
"
- Template E: Postmortem kickoff (post rollback or on completion)
"
:clipboard: Postmortem kickoff: ROLL-1123 — summary here. Timeline, root cause hypotheses, next steps, and owners. Link to raw logs and eval set attached. Please add notes in the thread.
"
Comms etiquette (recommended)
- Keep channel focused; use threads for investigations.
- If you’re posting a manual rollback, include timestamp and who executed it.
- Don’t escalate to page unless Red rule met. Use the steward gate.

Lightweight check-ins for A/B slices (when running multiple buckets)
- Add a runbook table in ticket: bucket-id, percent, user-cohort, steward, expected traffic profile.
- Use a periodic automated snapshot (every 10m) to post deltas for key metrics; steward comments on anomalies.

Synthetic traffic plan (short)
- If external-facing experiments risk content safety, run a 10–15m internal synthetic sweep simulating the worst-case prompts before live traffic.
- Use recorded golden prompts and a small batch of random perturbations. Post artifacts in ticket.

Failure modes and quick mitigations
- Model-serving OOM: fallback to smaller model variant + reduce batch size. (SRE)
- Moderation cascade increase: immediate mute of canary route and gather samples for safety review.
- Latency degradation: check autoscaler, queue lengths, and trace for kernel spikes.

Post-activation wrap (30–120m after completion)
- Steward fills in short experiment log: what happened, decisions, anomalies, and next steps.
- Short alpha survey if internal cohort used: collect 3–5 qualitative notes.
- If rollout completed, schedule 1-week health check to watch for delayed regressions.

Templates for ticket fields (copy into Jira/experiment ticket)
- Hypothesis:
- Acceptance criteria (numeric):
- Primary signals (with dashboards/links):
- Rollback criteria (numeric thresholds + manual triggers):
- Steward + backup name/contact:
- Synthetic test plan link:

Open questions / TODOs (short list)
- Automate the Slack snapshot posting (bot) so stewards don't have to paste metrics manually.
- Create a small library of golden prompts per product vertical for quick evals.
- Decide whether safety reviewer must be on-channel for all English-language model changes or only high-risk launches.

Notes to self (drafty):
- This should be 1–2 pager that release stewards can memorize. Too many knobs and people will skip the ceremony.
- Try it on small infra change next week to workout timings.

If you use this doc: copy the templates, paste into the rollout ticket, ping the on-call, and set a two-line public summary in the product weekly.

End of doc."
